# tsurara

> tsurara generates types and one call function per operation from OpenAPI 3.0, 3.1 and 3.2 (and Swagger 2.0) for TypeScript, Python, Rust and Go. The generator is a single binary; generated code calls a small runtime library per language and returns Results instead of throwing.

- [README](https://github.com/tsurara-openapi/tsurara/blob/7c43bb18c3cbc4d44d58c4d5517b666325d04f97/README.md): what tsurara is, and a first TypeScript target

## Agents

- [tsurara](https://github.com/tsurara-openapi/tsurara/blob/7c43bb18c3cbc4d44d58c4d5517b666325d04f97/skills/tsurara/SKILL.md): tsurara generates types and one call function per operation from an OpenAPI definition. The generated code calls a small runtime (`@tsurara/client`, `tsurara-client` for Python and Rust, `github.com/tsurara-openapi/tsurara/runtimes/go`)....
- [Configuration](https://github.com/tsurara-openapi/tsurara/blob/7c43bb18c3cbc4d44d58c4d5517b666325d04f97/skills/tsurara/references/configuration.md): `tsurara.config.yaml` (or `.json`, `.toml`) at the project root; `docs/guide/configuration.md` in the tsurara repository (or the MCP resource `tsurara://docs/guide/configuration.md`) lists every key.
- [Go](https://github.com/tsurara-openapi/tsurara/blob/7c43bb18c3cbc4d44d58c4d5517b666325d04f97/skills/tsurara/references/go.md): Each operation is a function in the generated package: `ctx`, the client, required parameters, the body, then `*{Op}Options` (or `nil`). It returns `(*tsurara.Success[T], error)`; failures are `*tsurara.Failure[E]`.
- [Python](https://github.com/tsurara-openapi/tsurara/blob/7c43bb18c3cbc4d44d58c4d5517b666325d04f97/skills/tsurara/references/python.md): Each operation is a function in `operations/<name>.py` taking the client first and keyword arguments after it; it returns a Result object. The same function works with `Client` and, awaited, with `AsyncClient`.
- [Rust](https://github.com/tsurara-openapi/tsurara/blob/7c43bb18c3cbc4d44d58c4d5517b666325d04f97/skills/tsurara/references/rust.md): Each operation is an `async fn` in the generated `operations` module: required parameters are arguments, optional ones fields of `{Op}Options` (which implements `Default`). It returns `Result<Success<T>, Failure<E>>`.
- [TanStack Query and mocks (TypeScript)](https://github.com/tsurara-openapi/tsurara/blob/7c43bb18c3cbc4d44d58c4d5517b666325d04f97/skills/tsurara/references/tanstack-query.md): With `typescript.query: tanstack`, every operation also has options for TanStack Query 5 in `query/{function}.ts`, and with `typescript.mocks: msw` an MSW handler in `mocks/operations/{function}.ts`. Use them instead of writing a `queryF...
- [TypeScript](https://github.com/tsurara-openapi/tsurara/blob/7c43bb18c3cbc4d44d58c4d5517b666325d04f97/skills/tsurara/references/typescript.md): Each operation is a function `operationId(client, options)` in `operations/`, with types `{Op}Data` (its input), `{Op}Result` (every outcome) and the schema types in `schemas/`. Create one client per base URL and pass it explicitly.
